newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom, FCL Paper drag NZ shares down at close.
newsitem.headline: Telecom, FCL Paper drag NZ shares down at close.

text.p: * Falls in Telecom, FCL Paper, take NZ shares lower
* Market coasts in consolidation phase
* Fisher and Paykel up sharply on marketing initiative
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index -11.20 at 2,532.71
139 nil * NZSE-10 cap index -7.75 at 1,271.50
373 nil * NZSC cap index +0.43 at 5,265.79
349 -7 * NZMC cap index +4.29 at 2,020.23
405 nil * Volume NZ$58 million. Futures untraded
758 -6 * Other movers - +15 +4
Falls in Telecom and Fletcher Paper drove New Zealand shares lower at the close on Wednesday while the broader market was largely static.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index lost 11.20 points to 2,532.71 on turnover worth NZ$58 million. Telecom lost six to NZ$7.58 and Fletcher Paper eased seven to NZ$3.49.
"The market is coasting in a consolidation," Richard Burton at Cavill White Securities said.
"It's had a good run up so maybe we'll have three or four down days," he said.
Telecom's decline would come as a relief to many who considered the stock over-priced, brokers said.
FCL Paper lost seven to NZ$3.49 while FCL Forests eased four to $1.94, possibly due to higher interest rates.
Outside the top five Fisher and Paykel had a strong day, gaining 15 cents to NZ$5.75.
Burton said the price gain may be a reflection of behind-the-scenes marketing of the stock by F&P after the launch of its new "Dishdrawer" dishwasher.
The company has also put some effort into explaining the workings of its healthcare division.

But in general terms, concerns about corporate earnings remain. Carter Holt Harvey is to report its first quarter profit on Thursday and analysts expect a net profit in the order of NZ$45-50 million -- well short of a year ago.
Its shares dipped one cent to $3.72 by the close
